n7cd9b777443.s: Which was the first of Muhammad Ghori's conquests in India, taken in 1175?
n7cd9b777443.x: Ghori took Multan in 1175, then Peshawar (c. 1179), Sindh (c. 1182) and Punjab and Lahore (c. 1190).

n19bcaace52e.s: After the Arab conquest of Sindh, Hindus and Buddhists were given which status?
n19bcaace52e.x: The conquest did not cause mass Islamisation; Hindus and Buddhists were granted dhimmi status.

na7b3daecb55.s: Which historian linked Turkish success to 'Indian feudalism' - feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy?
na7b3daecb55.x: R.S. Sharma linked feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy to Turkish success; caste also restricted fighting to a few groups.

n625992a5a00.s: The traditional four Agnikula Rajput clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and:
n625992a5a00.x: The four Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki; the Chandelas are not on the traditional list.

ne2c089bb5be.s: In which year was the ASI survey of Bhojshala at Dhar ordered?
ne2c089bb5be.x: The ASI survey was ordered in 2024; 2003 is the year of the ASI arrangement for worship on separate days.

n679ec7aea4c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the periods covered by Persian chronicles?
o: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers a period earlier than Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
Tabaqat-i-Akbari covers the period up to Akbar's reign.
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi covers a period earlier than Taj-ul-Maasir.
n679ec7aea4c.x: The order of periods covered is Taj-ul-Maasir, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, Tabaqat-i-Akbari, so Taj-ul-Maasir is earlier than Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

ndfd20709b62.s: According to Telugu sources such as Pratapa Charitra, Warangal was invaded how many times?
ndfd20709b62.x: Telugu sources (Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa, Kaluvacheru) record eight invasions; Muslim sources record five.

new.s: Who wrote Taj-ul-Maasir?
new.x: Taj-ul-Maasir is by Hasan Nizami; Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

new.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by:
new.x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is the work of Minhaj-us-Siraj.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami, not Minhaj-us-Siraj; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni raid Nagarkot (Kangra) for its temple treasure?
new.x: Mahmud raided Nagarkot in 1009; Thanesar was 1014, Mathura and Kanauj 1018, Somnath 1025-26.

new.s: At which place did the Pratihara king submit to Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018?
new.x: At Kanauj (1018) the Pratihara king submitted to Mahmud.

new.s: Somnath was sacked by Mahmud in 1025-26 during the reign of the Solanki ruler:
new.x: The Somnath raid took place under Solanki Bhima I, not Bhima II; Mularaja II later defeated Ghori in 1178.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ghaznavids:
1. Alptigin was the founder of the Ghaznavid line.
2. Sabuktigin is called the real founder of the dynasty.
3. Mahmud aimed at a permanent empire in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Alptigin was the founder and Sabuktigin the real founder; Mahmud's raids were for plunder, not for a permanent empire.

new.s: Muhammad bin Qasim was the nephew and son-in-law of:
new.x: Qasim was the nephew and son-in-law of Al-Hajjaj, the Umayyad governor; Caliph al-Walid sent him.

new.s: Arab writers said which Indian dynasty had the strongest cavalry in India?
new.x: Arab writers credited the Pratiharas, whose Nagabhata I drove back the Arabs, with the strongest cavalry.

new.s: When Mularaja II defeated Muhammad Ghori in 1178, who acted as his regent?
new.x: Mularaja II (Bhimdev II) was a minor; his mother Naika Devi was regent when Ghori suffered his first defeat near Mount Abu.

new.s: The Battle of Chandawar (1194) was fought near:
new.x: Chandawar lies near Firozabad (UP), on the Yamuna near Agra; Tarain is near Karnal.

new.s: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by:
new.x: Edward Sachau translated Kitab-ul-Hind into English.

new.s: Utbi, court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni, wrote:
new.x: Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini (Tarikh-i-Yamini); Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin and Firdausi the Shahnama.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Turkish success:
1. North India lacked political unity after the Pratihara collapse.
2. The Turks relied on mounted archers against elephant-reliant Indian armies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: rival Rajput states lacked unity, and mobile cavalry with mounted archers beat elephant-based armies.

new.s: Who wrote Bisaldeva Raso?
new.x: Bisaldeva Raso, on Vigraharaja IV, was written by Narapati (Nalha); Jagnik wrote Alha Khand.

new.s: The play Lalita Vigraharaja was written by:
new.x: Somadeva wrote Lalita Vigraharaja on Vigraharaja IV.

new.s: Kirtikaumudi, about the Vaghela minister Vastupala, was written by:
new.x: Someshvara wrote Kirtikaumudi on Vastupala.

new.s: Who wrote Khuman Raso of Mewar?
new.x: Khuman Raso is by Dalpati Vijay, not Karnidan; Dungar Singh wrote Shatrusal Raso.

new.s: The Vimal Vasahi temple at Dilwara is dedicated to:
new.x: Vimal Vasahi (c. 1031) is dedicated to Rishabha; Luna Vasahi is dedicated to Neminatha.

new.s: The Luna Vasahi temple at Dilwara (1230) was built by:
new.x: Luna Vasahi was built by the Vaghela ministers Vastupala and Tejpal; Vimal Shah built Vimal Vasahi.

new.s: 'Old Somnath' temple was built in 1783 by:
new.x: Ahilyabai Holkar built Old Somnath in 1783; the present temple dates from 1951.

new.s: Who founded the Paramara dynasty?
new.x: Upendra (Krishnaraja) founded the Paramaras; Vasudeva founded the Chauhans, Nannuka the Chandelas and Mularaja I the Solankis.

new.s: The last Paramara ruler, killed in 1305 by Alauddin's forces, was:
new.x: Mahalakadeva was the last Paramara, killed in 1305.

new.s: The capital of the Kalachuris (Chedis) was:
new.x: The Kalachuris ruled from Tripuri near Jabalpur; Dhara was Paramara and Anhilwada Solanki.

new.s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar in Delhi is a work of the:
new.x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta work only moved to Delhi; it is not Anangapala's.

new.s: The jauhar of Rani Padmini of Chittor took place against:
new.x: Rani Padmini's jauhar at Chittor is linked to Alauddin Khalji's attack.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajput society:
1. Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights.
2. Rajput warfare relied mainly on guerrilla tactics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights; Rajput warfare was direct face-to-face combat, not guerrilla war.

new.s: The unfinished Bhojeshwar temple at Bhojpur, beside Bhoja's man-made lake, is dedicated to:
new.x: The Bhojpur (Bhojeshwar) temple in Raisen district is a Shiva temple with a huge linga.

new.s: Bhoja's Saraswati-Kanthabharana deals with:
new.x: Saraswati-Kanthabharana is on poetics and grammar; Samarangana Sutradhara is on architecture.

new.s: Which scholar supported the Kshatriya descent theory of Rajput origin?
new.x: G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya held the Kshatriya descent theory; Tod and Smith gave the foreign origin theory, Chand Bardai the Agnikula legend.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about medieval sources:
1. Foreign accounts supplement Indian texts.
2. Foreign accounts need no cross-checking with inscriptions and archaeology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian texts but must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.

new.s: Babur's memoir Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written in:
new.x: The Baburnama was written in Turki.

new.s: Who wrote the Humayun-nama?
new.x: Humayun-nama was written by Gulbadan Begum, Babur's daughter, at Akbar's request.

new.s: The Ain-i-Akbari forms which volume of the Akbarnama?
new.x: The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, dealing with administration and revenue.

new.s: Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama at the request of:
new.x: She wrote it at Akbar's request.

new.s: Who wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari?
new.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad; Badauni wrote Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.

new.s: Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin around 1350 at which court?
new.x: Abdul Malik Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin at the Bahmani court c. 1350.

new.s: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, on the Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah, was written by:
new.x: Yahya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi.

new.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri of Minhaj-us-Siraj comprises how many volumes?
new.x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri has 23 volumes and was translated into English by H.G. Raverty.

new.s: Sandhyakara Nandi's Ramacharitam tells the Ramayana together with the story of the Pala king:
new.x: Ramacharitam is a double-meaning poem on the Ramayana and the Pala king Ramapala.

new.s: Kalhana's Rajatarangini is divided into how many tarangas?
new.x: Rajatarangini, the 12th-century history of Kashmir, has 8 tarangas.

new.s: Hadikat-us-Salatin, a Persian chronicle of the Qutb Shahis, was written by:
new.x: Ali bin Tahir Bustani wrote Hadikat-us-Salatin; Zuberi wrote Basatin-us-Salatin.

new.s: Unlike Mahmud's bilingual coins, the coins of Iltutmish carried legends in:
new.x: Iltutmish's silver tanka and copper jital were purely Arabic; Mahmud's Lahore dirhams were Arabic plus Sanskrit.

new.s: The Vilasa copper plate (c. 1330) was issued by:
new.x: The Vilasa copper plate belongs to Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; the Kaluvacheru record belongs to Anitalli.

new.s: In Qutb Shahi calligraphy, the Nastaliq script was used for:
new.x: Nastaliq was used for Persian texts; Naskh was used for Quranic verses.

new.s: The Golconda manuscript 'Quliyat Quli' contains how many miniatures?
new.x: The Quliyat Quli manuscript has 14 miniatures.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biases in medieval chronicles?
o: Court histories tend to glorify the patron.
Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint.
Amir Khusrau was court poet of Alauddin Khalji.
Firishta's story of Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal is accepted by modern historians.
new.x: Modern historians reject Firishta's story of Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal.

new.s: Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara around 1420 during the reign of:
new.x: Nicolo Conti of Venice came c. 1420 under Deva Raya I; Abdur Razzaq came under Deva Raya II.

new.s: Duarte Barbosa, who wrote on Vijayanagara, came from:
new.x: Duarte Barbosa was Portuguese.
